item.title: Missing Illinois kayakers found dead near strait called Death's Door known for shipwrecks
item.description: David Thalman and Francesca Warick were likely not wearing life jackets when their bodies were recovered off Washington Island after kayaking Death's Door strait.
item.content:encoded:
The bodies of an Illinois couple, both 20, who had gone missing on a kayaking trip in Lake Michigan near a strait called Death’s Door in Wisconsin were recovered earlier this week.

David Thalman, 20, and Francesca Warick, 20, were found on Monday morning off Washington Island after they went missing over the weekend, according to a joint press release from the Door County Sheriff’s Office and Washington Island Police Department.

Washington Island is located across from the Door Peninsula. Kayakers leaving from the Door Peninsula must cross the Death’s Door strait, which is known for being turbulent, to reach Washington Island.

Authorities don't believe either one was wearing a life jacket.

10-YEAR-OLD BOY'S BODY PULLED FROM NEW JERSEY RIVER AS RESCUERS SEARCH FOR HIS SISTER

Hundreds of shipwrecks are believed to have happened in the notorious strait since the 19th century.

The Door County Sheriff’s Office said it had assumed command of the search after it turned into a recovery operation on Sunday.

Jane Lee, broker-owner of a RE/MAX office in Chicago suburb Lake Bluff, told FOX 32 that Thalman was a great employee.

"You don't see a lot of young people like that anymore today," she said. "He's very focused, always on time. We trust him 100 percent."

She said his family has a cabin on Washington Island and she started to get worried when he hadn’t answered her calls and texts about work after he left for the weekend.

FLORIDA KAYAKER'S GRISLY FIND IDENTIFIED AS WOMAN MISSING FOR DECADES - NOW COPS HUNT HER KILLER

"That moment I did worry," she said, adding that when her office heard the news, "We all cried. Everybody was in shock."

She added, "We feel a huge loss."

Warick, a twin, "brought joy to everyone around her," according to her obituary.

"She was a bright, happy, and free-spirited young woman whose beautiful smile and kind heart left a lasting impression on all who knew her. She loved her family deeply and treasured every moment spent with them."

Authorities said the couple likely drowned. Their deaths remain under investigation.

item.title: Caribbean hot spot gripped by water crisis, and tourists scramble to reschedule plans
item.description: San Juan faces 48-hour water outages, and Puerto Rico's severe drought has raised concerns for tourists visiting the island. Some travelers have canceled dream vacations.
item.content:encoded:
Puerto Rico is implementing water rationing measures in San Juan amid an intense drought, raising questions for American tourists visiting the Caribbean island.

More than 180,000 water customers will face 48-hour water outages on an alternating schedule starting Friday, according to The Associated Press.

Historical weather data shows July was the driest month for San Juan in more than 120 years and the second-hottest month on record.

CRUISES THROWN INTO CHAOS AS DROUGHT STRANDS SHIPS, LEAVES PASSENGERS SCRAMBLING

The U.S. Drought Monitor reports that nearly 25% of Puerto Rico is experiencing a severe drought and another 36% is under a moderate drought, according to the AP.

The situation is raising concerns among some tourists regarding upcoming trips to the island.

On a Reddit forum dedicated to travel to Puerto Rico, one tourist said that, though the tourist's hotel was equipped with an emergency water supply, the tourist was still worried about the shortage.

"Can someone please be realistic about what it’d be like to visit during this?" the Reddit user asked. "Will it affect restaurants and bars? Should we cancel even though we likely won’t get anything refunded?"

DISNEYLAND GUESTS LEFT SCRAMBLING AFTER WATER OUTAGE SHUTS BATHROOMS AND RESTAURANTS

In response, other users offered mixed assessments of how the rationing could affect visitors.

"Hotels have cisterns and generators," one person wrote. "However, you should prepare to be flexible in your outlook, as it is a crisis."

"Hotels are probably the ones less affected by all of this," a different Reddit user advised. "Businesses and restaurants will [definitely] have to adjust, like they've had to in the past. Droughts don't happen every year but they are common."

"Good luck is all I have to say," another person said. "Have family [that] were told about upcoming water shutoffs."

VACATION HOT SPOT FACES NEW CDC TRAVEL WARNING AS OUTBREAK CASES CONTINUE CLIMBING

Others were less concerned about how the drought could affect travelers.

Biggest "issues you’ll encounter [are] no ice in drinks, or car washes available," a Reddit user said.

"Pools are unaffected, restaurants might use paper plates," another said.

The person behind the original Reddit post later updated the thread to say the travelers canceled their trip.

"We didn’t feel good about going and canceled," the Reddit user said. "We got refunds on some things, not others, and hope to be back another time."

Water-related advisories have also affected travelers in other tropical destinations.

Earlier this year, officials in Hawaii issued multiple brown water advisories across the state's islands in the aftermath of a storm.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

At the time, there were concerns about heavy rain runoff carrying pesticides, sewage and animal waste into the ocean, which raised concerns about E. coli and salmonella.

"If the water is brown, turn around," the Hawaii Department of Health Clean Water Branch said.

The Associated Press contributed reporting.

item.title: The Colorado Buffaloes are once again getting roasted online for looking like a Pop Warner team
item.description: A new Colorado Buffaloes practice video has fans questioning the team's size, comparing Coach Prime's squad to a Pop Warner or high school team.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a while since I talked about the Colorado Buffaloes football team — their spring game, to be exact.

College football had been gone for three months at that point and every Power 4 program's spring game was basically like an oasis in a desert when it came to the cravings of the fans.

At that time, the Buffs were making headlines for the physical makeup of their team, and since no one else had anything to talk about, the mighty mites of Boulder got the microscope put squarely on them.

OKLAHOMA SOONERS QUARTERBACK JOHN MATEER LOOKS ABSOLUTELY JACKED JUST IN TIME FOR FALL CAMP

Folks on the internet picked Colorado apart for their lack of size, comparing them to a high school football team.

Now, summer workouts have concluded and fall camp is in full session, so let's check in on the Buffaloes and see what they've been doing in the weight room all offseason.

Surely Coach Prime had his guys in the lab getting jacked all summer long, right?

Hmm, that's weird. Why would the Colorado football official X account post a video of a local Denver-area Pop Warner team running passing drills?

MICHIGAN STATE'S SPRING GAME SHENANIGANS ARE A CRIME AGAINST HUMANITY

Oh, wait, I've just received an urgent update that says this is, in fact, the actual Colorado Buffaloes football team practicing for the 2026 season.

How awkward.

What exactly does the strength and conditioning coach do at Colorado, anyway?

It's not just me being a jerk, either.

The comments section under the post is filled with people who are questioning why a Power 4 football team looks like a solid 6A high school program from Texas.

I was only half kidding when I questioned why the Colorado account was posting Pop Warner clips, too.

When I scrolled past this initially, all I saw was the size of the players and the field they were playing on, so I had to do a legitimate triple take to make sure what I was seeing was accurate.

For crying out loud, even the ref in the background looks like a high school student they got as a volunteer for a summer job.

Speaking of the Colorado X account, I feel bad for the social media admin in charge of posting this.

You know that young man or woman was thinking, "This is going to get us torched online."

And, you know what? They were absolutely right.

From everything I could find, the Buffs are projected to finish at or near the bottom of the Big 12, and without knowing too much about what the team has returning aside from former five-star signal caller Julian Lewis, I can see why.

Coach Prime better hope his players are as fast as he was when he played college football, because they certainly aren't overpowering any of their opponents this season.

item.title: It sounds like Tony Romo may never return to CBS
item.description: Tony Romo's OWI arrest may trigger a morals clause exit from CBS, but his $18 million annual contract through 2030 sets up a major legal battle.
item.content:encoded:
It sounds like Tony Romo may never return to CBS.

As OutKick reported last week, Romo's OWI arrest put his future in jeopardy beyond the initial indefinite suspension.

Even before his arrest, there were doubts about whether CBS would keep Romo as its lead NFL analyst beyond this season, especially with the network set to air the Super Bowl in 2028.

Romo's stock has also fallen considerably over the past three seasons, with critics pointing to his lack of preparation, goofy antics, and increasingly forced banter with Jim Nantz.

According to Puck News, Romo's arrest could expedite his departure. The outlet reported on Thursday that the consensus around the sports media industry is that "Romo won’t be back."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

CBS could also invoke a morals clause to fire Romo for cause over the arrest video. However, Romo is owed 18 million a year through 2030. Therefore, his legal team would almost certainly fight any attempt to void the deal.

Either way, CBS does not have to put Romo back on the air.

Romo's exit would open up one of the biggest jobs in sports media: calling games alongside Jim Nantz. J.J. Watt will replace Romo this season after a promising year in the booth. If Watt works well with Nantz, CBS would have every reason to consider keeping him there full-time.

READ MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE HERE

The Ellison-owned CBS also has deep pockets and could go after a bigger name ahead of the Super Bowl next season.

Troy Aikman, Kirk Herbstreit, and Greg Olsen all have contracts that expire after this season. Expect CBS to consider each of them.

Aikman is the most intriguing option and arguably the best NFL color commentator in the industry. That said, it would likely take around $25 million a year for CBS to poach Aikman away from ESPN.

Olsen is currently the No. 2 analyst at Fox, but possesses the talent to be a No. 1.

Herbstreit is more of a long shot. While he is Amazon's top NFL analyst, he is still best known for his work on ESPN's College GameDay and college football coverage. CBS no longer has the college football inventory to match that.

As for Romo, it's hard to imagine another network wanting him in the booth, even with more streamers adding NFL games to their lineups.

item.title: Unearthed clip of El-Sayed revealing his 'hate' for iconic Michigan town sparks online firestorm: 'Dark heart'
item.description: A resurfaced clip shows Abdul El-Sayed saying he "hates" Mackinac Island, sparking viral backlash as he seeks Michigan's Democratic Senate nomination.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is facing pushback online over a resurfaced clip in which he says he "hates" arguably the most treasured location in the state.

In the documentary clip from 2020, which resurfaced in a story by The Midwesterner Friday, El-Sayed walks through Michigan’s Mackinac Island during his failed run for governor.

"I hate Mackinac so much," El-Sayed said of one of the state’s most recognizable vacation spots, which sits on an island in Lake Huron between Michigan's Upper and Lower peninsula's.

"It’s funny cause, like, if we win, this is gonna be, like, the summer home," El-Sayed added, referencing the governor’s summer residence on the island.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED RECOUNTS SMASHING VODKA BOTTLE AFTER BEARD CRITICISM

"I’m just gonna be like every time I’ve ever come here. I’ve hated it. Why am I here?"

The clip went viral on social media Thursday with conservatives blasting El-Sayed for looking down on the quaint village town.

MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS

"The rising stars of the Democrat Party loathe America and seek to destroy it," Federalist editor-in-chief Mollie Hemingway posted on X. "And unlike their spiritual forebears, they see less of a reason to hide it for political gain. "

"I got engaged on this island," Outkick founder Clay Travis posted on X. "It’s an awesome place. Honestly, I don’t understand how anyone could hate northern Michigan in summer, absolutely beautiful, most underrated spot in the country."

"Wow hating Mackinac!" former Trump advisor Steve Cortes posted on X. "A place that is so iconic to Michigan, to America. Abdul has a dark heart."

"Abdul el-Sayed is a repellent terror-loving anti-Semite--and that's not even the worst thing about him," Commentary Magazine editor John Podhoretz posted on X. "He hates Mackinac Island, one of the most wonderful places on earth. A person who hates Mackinac Island has had his soul ripped from his body."

"He would rather summer at his property in Dubai," National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) spokesperson Sarah Gallagher posted on X.

"Bro has no soul," On Brand Strategies communications associate Carly Moran posted on X. "It’s literally Heaven on Earth."

"Abdul speaks fondly of his Egyptian summers yet he shows utter disdain for one of Michigan’s most beautiful summer destinations," former Michigan GOP gubernatorial candidate Tudor Dixon told Fox News Digital. "He wants his history to be respected but belittles Michigander’s favorite memories. He doesn’t respect us, and, therefore, he cannot represent us."

"Abdul El-Sayed hot mic: 'I hate Mackinac so much,'" conservative influencer account End Wokeness posted on X. "This is the most American place in MI."

Some, including journalist Brad LaPlante, defended El-Sayed’s comments as being taken "out of context."

"El-Sayed was talking about the Mackinac Policy Conference, an annual gathering of policy pros and insiders that he argues brings together well-connected and powerful people and shuts most voters out of politics," LaPlante wrote.

Others weren't so sure, including Michigan Young Republicans board member James Asher, who responded in a post on X, "Brad, are you dizzy from the way you’re spinning this?"

Mackinac Island is beloved in large part because it has retained a character increasingly rare in American tourist destinations. Motor vehicles have been largely prohibited since the 1890s, leaving visitors to travel by foot, bicycle or the island’s famous horse-drawn carriages.

The island has Victorian homes, historic hotels, waterfront streets, natural scenery and celebrated fudge shops which draw more than a million visitors from around the world each summer, while landmarks such as the Grand Hotel and Fort Mackinac have helped make the island an enduring symbol of Michigan history and culture.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed’s campaign for comment but did not receive a response.

El-Sayed responded to the post from End Wokeness on Friday afternoon saying, "Not sure about 'End Wokeness,' but I don’t think the most 'American place in MI' can be a place that…bans cars."

item.title: Tennessee Titans revamped their mascot and social media certainly had some thoughts
item.description: The Tennessee Titans unveiled a revamped T-Rac mascot with a more realistic raccoon look, and social media had strong opinions about the makeover.
item.content:encoded:
It's a time of change for the Tennessee Titans. The team has a new stadium getting ready to open next year, and recently showed off some new threads that really scream, "Yeah, we used to be the Houston Oilers. What of it?"

So, with so much change, reimagining and upgrading happening within the organization, apparently they decided that the team's mascot, T-Rac, an anthropomorphic raccoon, needed a makeover as well.

And, as you may have expected, the citizens of social media had some thoughts.

JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS

Now, while the T-Rac revamp had likely been in the works for quite some time, the Titans couldn’t have picked a better time to unveil it.

Why? Because raccoon stock has never been higher, what with internet sensation Jimothy taking over to the point of getting his own theme night at a Seattle Mariners game.

So, now people are really into raccoons, even if all they usually do is pick through garbage bins and spread the contents all over the alley behind my house.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But, to that point, fans have strong feelings when it comes to the change, and while some liked T-Rac 2.0, his more realistic look was not met with unanimous approval online.

I can see both sides of this one.

On one hand, it seems like a waste of breath to get worked up over the mascot.

On the other, I still haven't forgiven the AHL's Hershey Bears for making their mascot, Cocoa, all trim and fit, instead of fat and jovial like he was in my youth.

That happened like fifteen years ago.

I feel like this is always the reaction to a new mascot. I mean, for the first 24 hours that Philadelphia Flyers mascot Gritty existed, he was reviled.

Then he fell on the ice, shot a Rangers fan with a T-shirt cannon, threatened to kill the Pittsburgh Penguins mascot, and — what do you know? — he practically became a god in Philadelphia.

I think it's just a matter of time before all Titans fans are willing to take a bullet for T-Rac 2.0...

...unless this season gets off to a bad start, in which case he might become the scapegoat (scaperaccoon?).

item.title: James Carville predicts 2028 Democratic primary will test true strength of party's socialist wing
item.description: James Carville says 2028 Democratic primary voters will decide the party's future direction, warning of a schism if the DSA wing takes power.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville told Fox News Digital that 2028 will decide the future of the Democratic Party, not 2026, saying all he can do is try to advise them not to make the wrong choice.

In recent months, there has been a rising faction of far-left Democratic candidates winning primaries in multiple states, and some more moderate figures are alarmed.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," Carville said on "The Sunday Briefing" referring to a streamer who has made controversial statements like claiming America deserved 9/11, something he later backtracked on. "If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy."

In the following days, Carville spoke to Fox News Digital about how the party stands at a historic crossroads. But he advises that 2028 will be the real test of the far-left's strength.

DEMOCRATIC STRATEGIST JAMES CARVILLE SAYS HE COULD BECOME A REPUBLICAN UNDER ONE MAJOR CONDITION

"This I believe 100 percent — the future direction of the Democratic Party is going to be decided by Democratic primary voters in 2028," he said.

"Everyone claims they're the ascendant ring, alright, on the 2028 presidential election, and this can only be resolved at the presidential level. It cannot be resolved at the state level," he said. "And I am sure that there will be robust representation from the DSA ring of the party, whatever you want to call it. I'm sure there'll be a robust number of candidates from what I would call the governing wing of the Democratic Party, but you call it what you want."

He asserted again that this is a matter of politics that must be decided by the base of the party itself. The 2028 primary promises to be a crowded contest, with figures ranging from Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to Gavin Newsom to Pete Buttigieg to Kamala Harris to Rahm Emanuel among those expected to vie for the nomination.

"And this can't be solved through op-ed pieces, it can't be solved through cable TV network packages, panels, it can only, and that's the way it should be, that the Democrats themselves have got to settle on the direction of their party, and they're going to have all the options, and we'll see just how popular this is," he said.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

When later asked about what would happen if the democratic socialist wing takes power, he repeated his past prediction that there will have to be a "schism" in the official party.

"I'm going to let Democratic voters determine the direction the party goes in, and if it goes in the direction of — I'm pretty confident it won't, but if it goes in that direction, then I'm going to be 82. OK, fine, go ahead, but not with me," he said. "Until Democratic voters choose the direction of the party, I'll try to do all I can to help them make the right choice, in my opinion."

item.title: ‘Sopranos’ stars reunite in emotional farewell for Vincent Pastore
item.description: Steven Van Zandt served as a pallbearer at Vincent Pastore's funeral, revealing he spoke to his "Sopranos" co-star just one day before his death.
item.content:encoded:
Years after "The Sopranos" came to an end, its stars reunited for a heartbreaking reason — to say goodbye to Vincent Pastore.

Pastore was laid to rest Thursday in New York, surrounded by family and friends. His "Sopranos" co-star, Steven Van Zandt, served as a pallbearer, helping carry the late actor to his final resting place. Pastore's casket was draped with an American flag in honor of his time serving in the Navy.

Pastore's daughter remembered the man best known for the role of Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero as "a giving person."

"He was a man who lived out his dreams … but he knew how lucky he was," she said during the emotional funeral, Page Six reported.

'THE SOPRANOS' ACTOR VINCENT PASTORE DEAD AT 80

"I think that’s why he tried to share as much of it with as many people as possible," she added. "Whether that was a big tip, always in cash, or by shaking hands with every cop on every corner."

Van Zandt told the outlet he kept in touch with Pastore "quite often" before his death.

"We just happened to call him two days ago. The day before he died, we luckily just happened to call him," he said, referring to him and wife Maureen. "He was one of a kind, and we’ll miss him very much."

Days after his death, the actor's "right-hand man," Stephen Villano, told the Post Pastore was nothing like the character he often portrayed on the screen.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"He said, ‘I’m an actor. I play a character.’ So, people would think that this is the man, but that wasn’t the man," he said. "The man was generous, he was kind, he was caring," Villano said.

"He cared about his neighbors, he cared about charities, he cared about fundraisers."

Villano said Pastore supported veterans in the Bronx, U.S. troops and the police department.

"He supported St. Jude’s [Children’s Research Hospital], and he supported the NYPD," Villano added. "Widows, orphans, their Christmas parties … all the time, back the blue."

Pastore died Aug. 1.

"Vinny passed away either yesterday or today at home in The Bronx," his manager, Robert Attermann, said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I had the privilege of representing Vinny for more than 30 years, long before 'The Sopranos' made him a household name," he added. "To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable 'Big Pussy,' but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more."

In addition to Pastore's role on "The Sopranos," the actor also appeared in "Blue Bloods," "Law & Order," "General Hospital," "Bull," "Pair of Kings," "Hawaii Five-0" and most recently lent his voice on an episode of "Yellowjackets."

He also appeared in a number of movies, including "Goodfellas," "A Bronx Tale," "Carlito's Way," "Gotti," "Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn," "Mickey Blue Eyes" and others.

"He loved being an actor," Attermann said. "He was passionate about his craft and was always encouraging, respectful and generous with young actors, taking the time to offer guidance and support whenever he could."

Fox News Digital's Lori Bashian contributed to this report.

item.title: Beachgoers warned after deadly 'flesh-eating' bacteria kills 5 in southern state
item.description: Five deaths in Louisiana from Vibrio vulnificus mark a sharp rise, as all nine cases involved open wounds exposed to warm seawater this year.
item.content:encoded:
A potentially deadly "flesh-eating" bacteria has killed five people in Louisiana this year, a sharp rise from the state’s typical death toll.

Health officials are warning beachgoers to take extra precautions before heading into the water.

Vibrio vulnificus is part of a wider group of Vibrio bacteria. Found primarily in warm, coastal waters, it can cause serious, potentially life-threatening infections when contaminated seawater enters an open wound, according to the CDC.

DEADLY BACTERIA FOUND IN WATERS NEAR LUXURY VACATION DESTINATION AHEAD OF SUMMER

Infections can also occur when someone eats raw or undercooked shellfish, especially oysters.

The Louisiana Department of Health has reported nine cases and five deaths so far this year. All nine cases were linked to people entering seawater with open wounds, and all of the infected patients had existing medical conditions, officials said.

In previous years, the state has averaged seven cases and one death.

Vibrio bacteria are found in higher numbers from May to October, when water temperatures are warmer, the health department noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Although infections are rare, Vibrio vulnificus can cause an illness called vibriosis, often marked by vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain, as well as potentially severe skin infections.

"People with severe infections may require intensive care or limb amputation," Louisiana health officials warned. "About one in five people with Vibrio vulnificus infection dies, sometimes within a day or two of becoming ill."

Initial signs and symptoms of a Vibrio skin infection include fever, redness, pain, swelling, warmth, discoloration and discharge, per the CDC.

While healthy people generally experience only mild symptoms, those who are immunocompromised or have chronic liver disease can face serious health risks.

If Vibrio vulnificus enters the bloodstream, it can cause advanced illness marked by fever, chills, septic shock and blistering skin lesions.

Some severe cases can cause an infection called necrotizing fasciitis, which is when the flesh around an open wound dies, the CDC cautions. This rare side effect has led to Vibrio vulnificus being described as "flesh-eating bacteria."

The bacterial infection is diagnosed by testing cultures obtained from stool, wounds or blood, according to health officials.

For mild infections, the CDC recommends increasing fluid intake to prevent dehydration.

Those with severe or prolonged infections should receive antibiotics to improve survival rates.

For patients with infected wounds, surgery may be necessary to remove dead tissue.

About one in five people will die from the infection, sometimes within a day or two of becoming ill, the CDC states.

Health officials caution against entering warm saltwater or brackish water if any fresh cuts, scrapes or wounds are present.

It’s also recommended to avoid consuming raw oysters and other raw shellfish, and to avoid cross-contamination of other foods with raw seafood or its juices.

Protective gloves should be worn when handling raw shellfish.

Those with liver disease, cancer, diabetes, HIV or thalassemia (a group of hereditary blood disorders) — as well as those who are taking immune-suppressing medications — are at a higher risk of complications and should take extra precautions, the CDC warns.

item.title: The men who fled these socialist regimes have a terrifying warning
item.description: Three immigrants who fled Venezuela, Cuba and the Soviet Union describe the nightmare of socialism, from blackouts and censorship to lost freedom.
item.content:encoded:
In the midst of sunshine and a summer breeze, in the land of the free and home of the brave, sit three men, all immigrants who fled their "Third World" countries running on the "nightmare" of socialist policies. 

"The record in my city was once that we ha[d] three days long without electricity. There were shortage[s] of water like every day. … It's a disaster," Emmanuel Rincón, who fled Venezuela in 2017, told Fox News Digital. 

"If you live in the USA … you are never going to experience that, and you're never going to be able to understand that.

"I have spent almost all my life under the Chavismo [Hugo Chavez] rule, and my family were always in opposition of the regime. So, I always understand the nightmare that socialism is."

TRUMP EXPANDS CUBA SANCTIONS BEYOND US COMPANIES IN MAJOR CRACKDOWN ON FOREIGN ENABLERS

"In Cuba, there is no water, no electricity, no freedom, no food, no salary, no clothes, no shoes, nothing," Eliécer Ávila, a Cuban immigrant living in Florida who fled the island in 2017 said. 

"And the little that there is is what [families living in the U.S.] send from here."

Ávila and his family were heavily censored, and they were fired from their jobs and banned from Havana, the capital of his home island, after a video was leaked to the BBC of him asking a series of "uncomfortable questions" to Ricardo Alarcón.

Alarcón is the former minister of foreign affairs in Cuba who was, at the time, the president of the national assembly of the country.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15M WAR ON DSA AFTER SOCIALIST PRIMARY WINS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

"I was persona non grata inside the capital in my own country. From there, I started a movement of young people and students that were pro-democracy … which put me in jail more than 40 times," Ávila shared.

During that time, he was invited to a Latin American Studies Association (LASA) event with activists and human rights defenders from around the world. 

"After I came back [from that trip], the dictatorship didn’t let me enter back in, and they put me in one of the 50 most wanted terrorists. Me, who doesn’t even have a traffic violation, just because I wanted freedom for Cuba," he said.

EXPERT WHO FLED CUBA WARNS OF ‘VICIOUS CYCLE’ THAT WILL LEAD TO ‘COMMUNISTS IN DOUBLE DIGITS’ IN CONGRESS

Gene Maine, an immigrant who escaped the Soviet Union with his mother in 1981, expressed a similar sentiment. 

"[Growing up] I started noticing that all the propaganda on TV — the two channels that we had — didn't look right. It seemed like it was a lie. We grew up in what turned out to be the Third World," Maine said.

"All the trumpeting on the street of how great this is, how this is the best, how evil America is, how evil Western Europe is and how evil capitalism is. People realized that they couldn't speak freely.

"There was no religion. The only religion allowed was communism, which is a religion. Let's not have any doubts about it. It is a religion, it replaces Christianity, Judaism. That's the environment I grew up in," Maine said.

"These are not only dictators. They are also narco-terrorists. These are really dangerous people," Rincón added about Venezuela.

"I ha[d] to take out all my family from Venezuela. This is my history, but there are millions of histories like this in Venezuela. These are the things that the people in the USA (don't) really understand about socialism."

item.title: Former DNC Vice Chair David Hogg claims Democratic moderates 'don't have the right values'
item.description: Former DNC Vice Chair David Hogg told moderate Democrats they "don't have the right values" as progressive candidates score primary wins before 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Former Democratic National Committee Vice Chair David Hogg told moderate Democrats they "don't have the right values" Thursday during an appearance on "The Source," arguing the party establishment is repeatedly losing because its priorities are out of step with Americans as progressive candidates score primary victories ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Hogg made his sharpest criticism after host Kaitlan Collins asked what he would tell moderates concerned that progressive nominees could struggle against Republicans in general elections.

"The reason why the establishment of our party is being defeated over and over and over again is because they don't have the right values that are aligned with not the Democratic base, but the American people," Hogg said. "Where people are sick and tired of listening to Democrats and tell them all the reasons why they can't solve their problems."

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Hogg told moderates they needed to change their approach rather than ask successful progressive candidates to move toward the center.

"I would say to the moderates in our party, 'You need to figure out how to actually offer something new to voters that isn't just the same message that you gave them in 2024,'" Hogg said.

Steven Bonnell II, the liberal streamer known as "Destiny," pushed back on Hogg's assessment in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying he does not believe the former DNC official represents rank-and-file Democrats.

"I would say that this is outside of the Democratic Party's mainstream views," Destiny said. "Polls seem to evidence this, with a plurality (or majority, in some cases) of Democratic voters feeling as though the party has moved too far to the left."

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

Destiny, who has repeatedly criticized the party's far-left socialist wing, said Hogg's comments were an example of a dynamic that allows progressives to attack moderates without facing similar scrutiny from within the party.

"People in the Democratic Party's extreme fringe have created a ‘ratchet effect,’ where you cannot criticize anyone to the left-of-moderate view point," Destiny said. "Those same people can infinitely attack the moderate wing, leading outsiders (and even people from within) to view the Democratic Party as far more extreme than it actually is."

He warned that a Democratic Party that decides its moderates do not share its values could face consequences at the ballot box.

"I think it would mean the Democratic Party would probably have a hugely difficult time succeeding in the upcoming general in 2028 and possibly even stumble in 2026," Destiny said. "Which is especially ridiculous given how low Trump's popularity is at the moment."

SEN MARK KELLY WARNS FAR-LEFT POLICIES THAT ‘DON’T MAKE SENSE’ COULD COST DEMOCRATS SEATS

Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville has taken the opposite side of the party's ideological battle, telling Fox News Digital Thursday that Democratic primary voters would ultimately reject the socialist wing.

"I think it's more likely than not that the Democrats embrace sanity," Carville said.

Carville said a takeover by the socialist wing could ultimately fracture the party, reiterating comments he has made amid the growing influence of figures including self-described socialist streamer Hasan Piker.

"That probably would result in some kind of schism in the party," Carville said. "I'm going to let Democratic voters determine the direction that party goes in, and if it goes in the direction — which I'm pretty confident it won't — but if it goes in that direction, then I'm going to be 82. OK, fine, go ahead, but not with me."

Carville has also said he would leave the party if Piker became a significant force within it, while Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., responded that Carville could "start his own party."

Fox News Digital reached out to the DNC for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Fox News Digital's Alexander Hall contributed to this article.

item.title: Duke Law's alleged race-based admissions accused of defying Supreme Court ruling: DOJ
item.description: Duke Law School allegedly gave Black applicants 3.5 times higher admission chances than Asian applicants with the same credentials, the DOJ says.
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department is accusing Duke University School of Law of favoring Black and Hispanic applicants over White and Asian applicants with the same academic records in its admissions process, which the Trump administration argues the law school used to meet its "diversity goals."

"Duke Law School doesn’t get a free pass to discriminate against white and Asian students simply because it thinks it has good intentions," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division said.

In 2023, the Supreme Court ruled in Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard (SFFA) that it was unconstitutional for colleges and higher education institutions to consider a student's race in their admissions processes. The decision prompted the Trump administration to open investigations into alleged race-based discrimination at dozens of colleges and universities.

JUSTICE DEPARTMENT ZEROES IN ON UCLA FOR ALLEGED ILLEGAL DEI ADMISSIONS AS ELITE SCHOOL CRACKDOWN EXPANDS

The Civil Rights Division, which began investigating Duke Law in April 2025, found that Black applicants who applied in 2025 had roughly 3.5 times the chance of admission as Asian applicants with the same academic credentials, according to a Justice Department letter sent to Duke Law. Investigators found that the median LSAT score for accepted Black applicants was lower than the median score for rejected Asian and White applicants.

"This consistent difference in the test scores between students of different racial groups is substantial and cannot be explained by a coincidence," the letter stated. "The magnitude and durability of these preferences across multiple cycles (including post-SFFA) confirm intentional discrimination."

The Trump administration’s review of internal communications found that the law school began preparing for the Supreme Court’s SFFA ruling so its admissions process could continue "to meet the Law School's goals for a broadly diverse student body."

For instance, Duke Law's post-SFFA guidance for admissions allowed officials to "consider applicants' discussion of how race affected their life, be it through discrimination, inspiration, or otherwise." Applicants provided these discussions in short-answer essays, where admissions officials could then "tag" the responses to provide context for weaker academic records when evaluating applicants.

COAST GUARD ENDING RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS FOR OFFICER COMMISSIONING PROGRAM UNDER TRUMP DEI CRACKDOWN

Duke Law states that it values "students with a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and interests that may not be directly related to their legal ambitions," encouraging applicants to "highlight different elements" of who they are.

"Using ‘diversity’ essay questions to identify preferred races for admission is still illegal discrimination based on race, and this Department is committed to eliminating it everywhere we find it, including in our nation’s law schools," Dhillon said in a statement.

After SFFA, Duke Law admissions continued to release reports highlighting the school's diversity and its efforts to achieve "race-neutral" admissions standards. In a May 2024 annual review, the associate dean of admissions highlighted the diversity of the incoming fall 2023 class, including the number of Latino, Black and Asian or Asian American students.

In the school's 2025 Annual Review Memorandum, the admissions dean suggested that the law school can gauge the diversity of its student body by observing students on campus rather than compiling formal statistics.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

A Duke University spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the university is aware of the Justice Department's allegations.

"The Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division issued a letter of findings related to Duke Law’s admissions practices. We are reviewing the letter and its conclusions carefully. Duke is committed to complying with the law and will continue to do so in a manner that is consistent with our academic mission," a Duke University spokesperson said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for additional comment.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Title IX defender Payton McNabb praises Sophie Cunningham, reacts to Caitlin Clark
item.description: Payton McNabb applauds Sophie Cunningham's courage, rips Cheryl Reeve's trans inclusion stance, and explains why Caitlin Clark's voice matters.
item.content:encoded:
Long before Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham challenged the conversation surrounding women's sports, Payton McNabb was living its consequences.

A high school volleyball match changed McNabb's life. Years later, she sees Cunningham taking on a fight that has followed her all the way to Capitol Hill.

WATCH PAYTON MCNABB'S FULL INTERVIEW WITH OUTKICK:

After suffering a traumatic brain injury and partial paralysis on her right side from a ball spiked by a biological male opponent, McNabb took her fight from a North Carolina volleyball court to Washington, where she has testified before lawmakers in defense of women's sports and Title IX.

JD VANCE PRAISES SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FOR 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISM

Now 21, McNabb sees that same battle reaching the WNBA and believes the league's response is exposing a glaring double standard.

Speaking exclusively with OutKick, McNabb applauded Cunningham for taking a stand, ripped Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve over her support for transgender inclusion and explained why Caitlin Clark's voice could carry enormous weight with the next generation of female athletes.

"I started speaking out when I was 18," McNabb told OutKick. "I'm 21 now, but within the last few years, why have I had to go in front of Congress and explain that there's a biological difference between a man and a woman? It makes no sense, and it sounds like such a dumb argument."

Cunningham's willingness to speak out has particularly impressed McNabb, especially as the Fever guard's profile has soared.

"What we've seen through Sophie Cunningham has been so courageous," McNabb said. "I just applaud her so much because it takes a lot to say this, unfortunately, and it shouldn't, but it does."

"For her to say it now and not wait until it's safe ... and her career is really taking off, I think it just adds a whole other layer on top of how special it really is," McNabb continued. "We don't really have a lot of big-name athletes willing to say it, and that's really unfortunate, but that's just the way it is. But it's because of how they get treated."

McNabb pointed to the backlash Cunningham has received as evidence of that risk.

"She's getting vilified or villainized for literally just saying what everyone already knows and thinks, but are just too afraid to admit," McNabb said. "It's just crazy because there wouldn't be a WNBA. We wouldn't know who [Lynx coach] Cheryl Reeve is or even Sophie Cunningham or any of these girls if it wasn't for Title IX."

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

McNabb had far less praise for Reeve, who has publicly defended trans participation in sports and wore a Trans Kids Belong shirt during a matchup against Cunningham and the Fever to prove it.

"It just seems like women like Cheryl Reeve who were fighting against other women and girls, I just will never understand that," McNabb said. "You have little girls who are showing up to the game and excited about their favorite player standing up for them and wanting the same opportunities that she has to be in place for them. And the coach seems to be pulling up the ladder."

McNabb called out the glaring hypocrisy of demanding empowerment for female athletes while simultaneously opening the door for biological men to take their spots.

"You can't complain on one hand about not getting as much as the men or not getting as many opportunities or viewers ... and then on the next, you're encouraging men to take over the very category you're wanting separate from them," McNabb said.

McNabb predicted the league's virtue signaling will evaporate the second a biological male steps onto a WNBA court and forces players to face reality.

McNabb pointed to Julie Tétart, a 6-foot-3 biological male dominating a French women's league who (with the help of OutKick's Joe Kinsey and founder Clay Travis) recently signaled interest in making the jump to the WNBA.

"I think it's gonna have to take this dude from France to come in here and like dunk on Angel Reese and then maybe they'll be like, 'Oh, maybe this isn't allowed,'" McNabb said. "I don't know. It's going to have to affect them personally."

Make no mistake: McNabb isn't rooting for biological men to wreck the WNBA. She wants these athletes protected, even if they won't fight for themselves.

CLAY TRAVIS SETS SIGHTS ON FRENCH TRANS PHENOM JULIE TETART FOR PROPOSED 'INCLUSIVE' WNBA EXPANSION TEAM

"Of course, I don't want that to happen," she said. "I'm fighting for the girls that are even going against us because I want them to have the protections and the opportunities whether they like it or not."

McNabb challenged the league's progressive establishment to put its money where its mouth is: if biological males belong in girls' high school athletics, they belong in WNBA coaching spots, too.

"I want transgender coaches," McNabb said. "I think that there should be a transgender coach taking Cheryl Reeve's place because that will be just as much of a woman as she is. ... If they're saying this is okay for the high school girls, then it should be okay for them."

Then there's Caitlin Clark.

THE LEFT WANTS CAITLIN CLARK, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TO SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE WHEN IT COMES TO TRANS SPORTS

McNabb understands why the Fever superstar has largely kept the focus on basketball rather than wading into another contentious issue.

"She gets a lot of backlash for literally no reason, from jealousy," McNabb said. "I could imagine not wanting more of that would probably be ideal."

Still, McNabb believes Clark's enormous influence makes her part of the Title IX debate whether she addresses it publicly or not.

"Whether Caitlin Clark likes it, she's a part of the conversation, and it would just mean so much to the next generation," McNabb said. "To all the little girls in the stands that are wearing number 22, it would mean a lot to them."

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

Few voices in women's basketball, McNabb argues, could carry more weight.

"She's the best player in the WNBA, and for her to be able to take a stance and say something, that would be huge," McNabb said. "She's where she is today because of Title IX, and she needs to be able to acknowledge that and accept that and want that for the next generation of girls."

For McNabb, the issue remains deeply personal.

More than three years after the volleyball injury that changed her life, McNabb said her health has finally reached a significant turning point.

"The doctors didn't know if I would ever get back to how I was, and they said it could take three years before I could see real progress," McNabb said. "It's so weird, because it actually took exactly three years for me to see a difference in coming back and bouncing back with my health."

The teenager who once failed public speaking has since testified before Congress and become an Independent Women ambassador, using the injury that changed her life to try to prevent other girls from enduring the same thing.

"I wasn't planning on going into politics, really had no idea what was going on at all," McNabb said. "I just had a genuine story that happened to a real person and affected a real family and community."

"I've really just tried to use the story to spread awareness in hopes no other girl has to go through what I went through."

item.title: Former NBA first round pick Enes Kanter Freedom declares for 2027 WNBA Draft

item.title: US Army offering defense firms 'concierge access' to test weapons at military ranges
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll says defense companies can now book military test ranges within 30 days through a new online portal with concierge access.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army is opening up military test ranges to private defense companies and promising "concierge" access aimed at dramatically cutting the time it takes companies to test new weapons and technologies.

Army Secretary Dan Driscoll told reporters in a call on Friday that companies will be able to secure testing opportunities within 30 days of submitting a request, compared with a typical wait of roughly 18 months.

"We just had to get out of our own way," Driscoll said. "And so the 30-day clock starts today. So if somebody goes to testrange.army.mil, submits it in the next hour, we will have you on a range within 30 days."

'A NEW KIND OF WAR': INSIDE UKRAINE'S HIDDEN FACTORIES MASS-PRODUCING COMBAT DRONES

The move is part of a broader Army effort to speed up the development and delivery of technologies including drones, counter-drone systems, long-range fires and low-cost interceptors.

"If you look at what is occurring all over the world today, if you look what Ukraine has done so incredibly well, it's this innovation through necessity and it's innovation at the speed that is near or close to matching the commercial sector," Driscoll said. "And so what we, the Army, are trying to do is break down every single barrier that we have put up over the last 20 and 30 years."

The Army is opening four stateside locations to industry: Dugway Proving Ground in Utah, West Cibola Range at Yuma Proving Ground in Arizona, Camp Shelby Joint Forces Training Center in Mississippi and Camp Grayling Joint Maneuver Training Center in Michigan.

PENTAGON PLOTS NEW NUCLEAR OPTIONS FOR TRUMP AS AMERICA’S BIGGEST ADVERSARIES RAISE STAKES: REPORT

The Army is also working with U.S. Africa Command and partners to provide industry access to the Multidomain Training Area in Morocco, according to an Army press release. Companies will be able to request test range time through a new online portal and will be assigned a dedicated "concierge" to help navigate the scheduling process. Companies do not need an existing federal contract or prior relationship with the U.S. government to apply.

"A company with a good idea shouldn’t need a team of lawyers and a program of record just to prove their equipment works," Driscoll said.

ANTARES REACHES REACTOR CRITICALITY UNDER TRUMP PILOT PROGRAM, MARKING MAJOR NUCLEAR MILESTONE

The ranges are intended to give companies access to realistic environments where they can rapidly test and refine emerging technologies, including under conditions resembling those encountered on modern battlefields.

The Army cautioned that submitting a request does not guarantee a company its preferred location or testing date because of capacity constraints, but said its concierge team will work with applicants to identify available testing windows and locations.

When Hannity asked whether Rabb, who boasts of running in the "bluest district in America," truly supports "amnesty for illegals" and abolishing national borders, the lawmaker replied, "What are illegals?"

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

Hannity responded, "Illegal immigrants: People that didn't respect our laws, borders and sovereignty … entered the country without permission."

Rabb said he didn’t accept the "premise" of the question.

"There are folks who have documentation. But these are not criminal acts," he said, adding that he "absolutely" wants to abolish ICE and "dismantle immigrant concentration camps."

"I want to end all deportations. We want to make sure that there's an immigration system that is fair, just and efficient, and we don't have that system," Rabb added. He went on to cite an immigration reform package led by Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., and former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema, D-Ariz., that he lamented "your president" successfully killed.

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

When asked about abolishing police as an institution — in line with socialist doctrine — Rabb said the statement was "interesting" because there were few or no organized police departments in early America.

"Ultimately, what we want is to have communities that are safe, and 99% of what police do are not going after the bad guys," he said.

Philadelphia did not organize its police department as a centralized municipal force until 1854. Before that, local elected constables and civilian watchmen patrolled their neighborhoods for crime. The Philadelphia Police Department formed after a series of riots, when what is now Philadelphia was divided between the City of Philadelphia and Philadelphia County, which are now coterminous.

"We need to keep our communities safe, and there were ways of doing that before the term ‘police’ ever existed," Rabb said.

On disarming police, a policy some socialists support, Rabb said he believes in "arming oneself," arguing that, as someone with Southern ancestry, the only way his family could protect itself was through self-defense.

"We couldn’t trust the police because they were largely part of the [Ku Klux] Klan," Rabb said. His paternal family roots trace to Columbus, Mississippi.

Rabb upset the Democratic establishment in his May primary, defeating state Sen. Sharif Street, D-North Philadelphia, the son of popular former Mayor John Street who also had the backing of incumbent Mayor Cherelle Parker and former Gov. Edward Rendell.

item.title: Trump says White House ballroom ruling jeopardizes lives of future presidents, vows Supreme Court appeal
item.description: Trump vows an immediate Supreme Court appeal after a federal appeals court ordered construction halted on his "massive" White House ballroom project.
item.content:encoded:
After a panel of federal judges ordered a halt to construction on the White House ballroom, President Donald Trump said he will immediately appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

In a Truth Social post Friday, Trump decried the 2-1 decision from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit as "horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful."

"The Circuit Court’s decision, which is totally wrong on the vital subject of STANDING, of which the plaintiff has none, severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House — including all future Presidents of the United States, and their families, as well as the lives of all those visiting, such as Heads of State and other Dignitaries, and all Americans who wish to visit the historic, beautiful Executive Mansion," Trump wrote in the post.

He also accused the court of refusing to acknowledge that the ballroom, which he said is being built ahead of schedule and under budget, "is a Gift from President Trump and Great Patriots of the United States of America."

TRUMP WARNS JUDGE AGAINST SACRIFICING NATIONAL SECURITY BY BLOCKING WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM, DRONE BASE

"There will be no expense to the American Taxpayer. This unjust decision must be overturned by the Supreme Court in its entirety," Trump wrote.

The appeals court on Friday upheld a lower-court decision that paused above-ground construction of the proposed 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom project, which replaced the demolished East Wing.

The earlier ruling allowed work to continue on underground national security facilities and certain safety and security measures, a decision the higher court also upheld.

The appeals court said in its 136-page ruling that the decision to build a "massive ballroom" lies with Congress, not with the executive branch.

REPUBLICANS EYE PICKING UP $400M TAB FOR TRUMP'S BALLROOM AS SOME DEMS OPEN TO 'DISCUSS' IDEA

Judges Patricia Millett and Brad Garcia wrote the majority opinion, remarking that there is no precedent for what Trump has done.

"We are aware of no instance in American history in which a President unilaterally and using privately collected funds demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now," they wrote.

The judges said their ruling does not prevent the president from building the ballroom if it is authorized by Congress in the future.

As Trump pointed out in his social media post, the ruling was stayed for 14 days to allow the defendants to seek a Supreme Court review.

It is not immediately clear if the Supreme Court will take up this case.

item.title: Blackjack losses, a chilling phone call and a diverted flight cap a chaotic Las Vegas vacation
item.description: David Hookstead's Las Vegas trip featured high-limit blackjack tables, Golden Tiki, Stage Door and machine guns while navigating threats in Las Vegas.
item.content:encoded:
*NOTE: Some names, locations, techniques and information have been withheld due to their sensitive nature.

You often don’t realize you’re in a fight for your soul until you’re deep in it.

As my loyal readers and viewers have realized, I have been fairly off the grid for roughly the past week.

Why?

It was time for my annual trip to Las Vegas, but unlike previous trips, this one was happening with the looming threat of the Iran War, death threats and the IRGC. Things were different for this working-class man this time around.

While I’m not going to get into specifics, there’s no question that due to a heightened alert status and ever-evolving threat matrices, precautions that never had been taken before were going to be necessary. It turns out some people aren’t fans of my outspoken ways, and unlike people who claim to be "threatened" by blue hair liberals (literally comical to even consider dangerous), being under the threat from a state-backed actor is a totally different ball game.

No box could go unchecked.

The first decision that was made was that I would move to the airport under the cover of darkness.

There are a couple of reasons why this was deemed the best option. First, it allows me to move when the city and airport aren’t buzzing yet.

Second, the streets being mostly empty provide far more tactical advantages than if they’re crowded and something goes wrong.

The plan didn’t survive me making it to the front door.

Immediately upon exiting the Hookstead Compound (location classified) with my bags, I spotted two military-age males that I’d never seen before. Keep in mind the entire point of the movements and schedule is that NOBODY is supposed to be around.

I know enough about the people who live in my vicinity to recognize most of them. I’ve never seen these two men in my life. It’s a shocking sight to behold, but they’re way more shocked to see me than vice versa.

A decision had to be made in a half of a second over whether or not this was finally it. Would the entire operation be aborted before entering the vehicle for the airport?

LUCKY TRAVELER WINS $3.3M JACKPOT ON 'WHEEL OF FORTUNE' SLOT MACHINE AT HARRY REID INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

Ultimately, sometimes the only way to fix a problem is to go clean through it (another lesson that some people would be wise to follow for Iran).

I closed the space quickly, deemed the two men not an immediate threat showing hostile intent and got on the move as quickly as possible.

As planned, the streets are completely empty and we’re able to get into the airport without issues. From that point, the goal was simple:

Blend in as much as possible, go unnoticed and get seated on the plane as quickly as possible. Every minute spent in the open at the airport is a minute where nobody is in complete control of the situation. That’s far from ideal.

Little did I know things would only get stranger from here.

I chose a seat as close to the cockpit as possible. Unusual for someone with my blue-collar roots? For sure, but a necessity given the stakes.

What seemed like a routine and normal flight became very different in a matter of seconds. For the first time in my life, I was on a plane where a metal gate was closed off up front by the cockpit without explanation.

That’s right.

There was a metal gate rolled out making the front portion of the plane an impenetrable fortress. I tried to get a look past the gate, but found it difficult. My only guess was that one of the pilots was out of the cockpit for some reason, but I was never able to confirm that.

Fortunately, the plane touched down without further incident.

The working-class man’s Las Vegas vacation was underway.

Just as quickly as I’d gotten on the plane to Vegas, I disappeared into the crowd blending in again. Nobody knows me, and I don’t know them. The less attention the better. We’re not chasing clout. We’re chasing demons that have haunted us for a long time, and doing it while operating to survive.

Things were about to get weird (noticing a trend) very quickly.

My driver appeared like a normal woman attempting to make small talk.

It was anything but normal.

For some unexplained reason, this woman starts talking to me about sex and a sex museum. At one point, she starts asking if I like sex.

Am I on a hidden camera show? Am I being pranked? I start making very measured and careful statements assuming whatever I say is absolutely being recorded. I can’t wait to get the hell out of this taxi as soon as possible. A working-class man might not have much in life, but we do have one thing:

Common sense, and common sense dictates asking a stranger about sex in a vehicle is about as strange as it gets.

I get out at the Cosmopolitan in Las Vegas with one clear goal in mind:

Get to the blackjack table as quickly as I can.

I dumped my stuff into my room, which for a working-class guy who had to fight for everything in life, I can tell you was pretty shocking. It featured a massive bedroom, a living room area, huge walk-in shower, a hot tub and a balcony overlooking Las Vegas.

I’m not going to lie to you all. It was epic. I guess life occasionally hands the downtrodden a win in life.

To the tables I went.

I pulled out a roll of working-class money and set it down at a blackjack table in the high-limit room. Now, some of you might be asking, "David, what is a guy like you doing in the high-limit room? That doesn’t seem like it’s your speed."

Fair question, and the answer is simple:

Privacy.

The high-limit room at the Cosmo is one of the nicest in Las Vegas, and it’s also fairly secluded.

Remember, I have significant threats I have to worry about, and unlike the unhinged clowns roaming around, the people who want me dead actually have the means to carry it out.

Head on a swivel.

I sit down at a double-deck table, and immediately go on a nice little run earning more money in a matter of minutes than a regular working-class guy does over the course of a few weeks.

When you don’t come from much, you know when to walk away with the win the universe gifted you (this energy won’t last for long). I push back from the table for the time being and keep the operation rolling.

Next stop? Stage Door for a hot dog and a cheap beer. The hot dog, while not amazing, is certainly worth the money and it’s also a tradition. It hits the spot, and I soon get word a second seasoned Las Vegas operator has arrived. For the sake of the story, he is identified as VO2. VO1, another seasoned Las Vegas operator, won’t arrive until the next day.

From here, things progress rather normally. We hit up the arts district for a couple beers and did a little exploring.

I was about to hit my next unexpected hurdle, and while I’m on a high alert status, I didn’t see this kind of roadblock coming.

I decide to head back for some more high-limit blackjack, and am promptly informed the casino needs extra information from me. I’m not going to share the specific information in a public setting, but it appears the amount of working-class money that I’ve put on the table in one day has possibly triggered some money laundering tripwires.

Me? The working-class guy from rural Wisconsin? You have to be kidding me.

After a brief conversation with the casino bosses, it’s smoothed over and the gambling continues.

Remember the win I had early in the day? That’s wiped out in about an hour, and then go ahead and tack on a few paychecks on top of that.

Now, this is where most people would start panicking. Those kinds of swings at the tables break most people, but most people aren’t from my rural Wisconsin background.

I’m in the fight, and while the IRGC hasn’t taken its shot yet, the casino is drawing financial blood.

Just like knowing when to walk away when you win, you also need to know when to not chase losses. I cut the cord, push back and live to fight another day.

I grab a burger on my way back to the room, crush it and pass out as soon as my head hits the pillow.

Day two started like any other day in Las Vegas. All was quiet in the streets and casinos and people were still asleep by the time I was on the move with enough caffeine in my system to kill a rhino. I guess I’m just built differently. If chugging Celsius was a skill, I’d be the Tom Brady of getting it done.

The day started with biscuits and gravy at Ellis Island, followed by getting kicked in the shorts at the blackjack tables. Fortunately, the losses this time around aren’t nearly as vicious, but it’s still not great. I’m now deep in a gambling hole. Not great, but it’s only a loss once you actually leave the city.

What happened next nobody could see coming…….most of all me.

The bat phone buzzes to life, and I see a name that stops me dead in my tracks. I know something serious must be happening for me to be receiving this call, and I now have a major issue:

I can’t take this call outside of a completely secure location.

My hotel room, which would get the job done, is too far away and time is of critical importance.

The decision is made for VO2 and myself to relocate to a closer secure location, and with the doorway secure, I answer the phone.

A serious flow of information starts flooding in.

Seconds feel like hours.

There are times when years pass without anything happening, and then there are times where decisions are made in seconds that can change everything.

This is the latter.

I try to process the information as quickly and as efficiently as I can, and it ultimately boils down to one call:

Go or don’t go.

You could hear a pin drop in the secure room. Based on the information I was hearing, I simply was not confident with going.

It’s a no go with the door left open for a decision to be made at a later time.

With my head spinning with a million thoughts, I get word that VO1 has touched down and is on his way to the rendezvous point. After a brief conversation, we head over to Ole Red (Blake Shelton’s establishment) for nachos and a beer.

The nachos were absolute fire. The best nachos I’ve ever had? No, but definitely very solid and delicious with some added brisket.

Next up was Golden Tiki in the Chinatown area of Las Vegas. Golden Tiki is another tradition every single year for us. It’s an outstanding tiki bar with a unique vibe, and some bathroom wallpaper that is a bit shocking at first sight. Seeing as how this is a family website, I won’t share further details. I have myself a couple tiki drinks, and both are well worth the money.

As a working-class guy, I can really only afford cheap domestic beers, but this is vacation. Let’s live a little. Plus, with the death threats, I simply can’t be living for the future. Much like fighting the demons, any day could be the last, and we’re leaving it all out on the field.

Now, there is one location in Las Vegas I’ve been more than eager to get to, and with the full trio locked in, it’s time to execute the plan.

Hogs & Heifers.

For those of you who don’t know, Hogs is an absolutely insane Las Vegas institution. It’s not for the faint of heart or easily offended. It’s a bar for true American patriots and it has the most entertaining bartenders in Vegas by orders of magnitude. They’ll insult you in the most vulgar way possible, but it’s all in the name of good fun.

It was closed last year, and that was the first time since discovering the gem that we weren’t able to go. That needed to change and it did.

It’s now located at the Plaza while its new permanent home is built.

The bartenders were as rowdy and fun as ever. While it’s an outpost location, it felt just like the old Hogs so many have come to know and love, and the Coors Banquets were as cold as ever.

Oh, did I mention the insults and jabs were flying in all directions? It felt good to be back, and as always, you meet some insane characters in there.

We rotate between playing blackjack and hopping in and out of the bar as the day stabilizes following the phone call in the secure location.

I’m actually feeling fairly good about it as I head back to my hotel room, but I’m also starving. I order room service and get hit with one hell of a surprise:

The full room service experience is a $160 minimum spend.

I honestly think what I’m hearing can’t possibly be true. I’m trying to order a wrap. I don’t need the full room service experience. Bring it to me in a bag and a plastic container and I’ll be fine. That’s exactly what ended up happening.

How is a working-class guy supposed to be able to afford a $160 minimum spend? It’s simply not possible. We’re lucky just to have food on the table. Forget the fancy stuff. Save that for the millionaires and billionaires, not guys like myself.

First, I have to operate under new procedures thanks to the Iranians. Second, I am gutted at the table. Third, I am reminded of just how blue-collar I am when ordering room service. The losses keep piling up.

Having said that, the wrap was delicious and the portion sizes were excellent.

Tuesday started just like any other day. I filmed a short war update and crushed a couple Celsius cans, and the vibes were high.

I’m also very excited for one very simple reason:

The schedule has a portion blocked off for letting it rip with some machine guns.

Generally speaking, I hate indoor shooting ranges and shooting ranges in general. I had a private outdoor one at my house growing up, and the idea of strangers with guns around me at a range has never been something I’ve really enjoyed. I know how good I am with a gun (most working-class men from Wisconsin can say the same), but I don’t know how good these random people are or what stupid stuff they might do. Add in the fact foreign tourists don’t know an AK-47 from a Beretta M9, and I think you get the point.

Well, when in Vegas, you do things you don’t do at home. I grabbed a PKM machine gun and PPSh-41 Soviet submachine gun.

Both were absolutely awesome. The PKM was shockingly light, and the rate of fire was exceptional.

The PPSh-41 was cool mostly because it’s the submachine gun the Soviets used in WWII against the Germans.

I wouldn’t say it’s a particularly impressive submachine gun or special, but it can’t be beat from a historical standpoint if you’re looking for foreign WWII guns. I can’t recommend both enough if you ever get a chance to shoot them. You won’t regret it. We also met some cool Welsh dudes at the range who absolutely loved America. It was a humbling reminder just how good we have it here in the USA. Foreigners would give anything to be part of our club, and none of us would give it up for anything.

Next, the trio filed over to El Cortez where I had a very mediocre bratwurst before, yet again, getting my wallet crushed at the blackjack tables.

I hope my wife is okay being solely responsible for the bills for the foreseeable future because this has turned into a catastrophic gambling nightmare.

What do you do when the world is against you and the demons are starting to sing? You numb the pain with a little Coors Banquet, and that’s exactly what we did by swinging by Hogs, where the bartenders were in rare form. I say that as a compliment. I can’t wait to visit next year once it’s in its final home. I can only imagine how glorious it will be.

The day wound down with a stop in the Arts District for a delicious espresso martini and some insanely good Mexican food, followed by a short stop at Ellis Island before closing beers at Stage Door. I eventually found myself back in the high-limit room with my blue-collar money (no money laundering concerns this time) and actually came out a little ahead. Slowly but surely, I’m crawling out of the hole I created.

However, my winning wasn’t the highlight of day three coming to an end. The dude sitting next to me at the table was hysterical. I legit couldn’t stop chuckling at every word coming out of this guy’s mouth, and a woman (I believe girlfriend but can’t say for sure) shows up and sits down next to him. Turns out she’s a former golf superstar and was at one point one of the top golfers in the world. Admittedly, I have no idea who she is, but I also couldn’t recognize any golfer other than maybe three or four. That’s a sport for rich people, and I’m anything but wealthy, no matter what the rumor mill says.

They were both a ton of fun, and then a Canadian showed up ripping cigs. What a night at the high-limit blackjack table. I wouldn’t have cared if I lost every penny because the dude was so funny that it made the whole thing entertaining, no matter the outcome. Fairly certain I also saw him tip several thousand dollars to the dealers in the time I was with him.

Day four was the final full day in Las Vegas, and after breakfast and some more blackjack, we decided to catch a ride to Fremont.

We’re not 50 yards down the street when the right front tire of the vehicle blows out, and the driver declares an emergency. It’s in the worst possible location. We’re nowhere near a parking garage or the safety of a building.

Is this how it ends for me? Have plans been set in motion that can’t be stopped?

I don’t know and I’m definitely not going to wait to find out. VO1 and I bail out of the vehicle, and I start scanning in all directions for threats. I don’t see anything, but we’re completely in the open and exposed. Nowhere to run. Nowhere to hide. I took a look at the guy’s vehicle, and as VO1 noted, "His right tire is f****d."

I peered over, and assessed the situation.

His right tire was completely destroyed. I don’t even understand what happened. I never heard a pop or any kind of blast.

It was fine when we entered the vehicle, and it was anything but fine now. Every second matters. The longer we stay exposed, the more risk we’re assuming.

A backup vehicle - a big black SUV - whisks in and we’re in it without hesitation racing towards where we’re going.

I still have absolutely no idea what happened with the original vehicle, and I doubt I ever will. Some questions are best left unasked.

We grab a couple beers and attempt to win some money. VO1 pulls an absurd four card blackjack split and hits it. The craziest part is it wasn’t the first time. He did the exact same thing earlier in the day at Ellis Island.

Two successful four card splits in one trip? Good luck replicating that at any point in the near future.

I also noticed at one point in the night that my phone all of a sudden had a crack in the screen protector, which VO2 and myself found extremely odd. It was never dropped and never left alone. None of us could explain it. Maybe there was a perfectly ordinary explanation. Maybe there wasn't. Either way, it became one more strange thing on a trip that seemed determined to keep getting stranger.

Fortunately, the night didn’t feature any more unexpected surprises, and instead focused on some honest conversations about some theories we have about relationships and life. Those aren’t my stories alone to share, so I won’t out of respect for the other parties involved.

I wake up, bang out another video update for the Hookheads (what my fans call themselves on YouTube) and grab a stack of cash to hit the high-limit room one final time before leaving.

That’s when there was an unexpected change of plans.

I’m well over a thousand miles from home, and I get a call learning that my HVAC system is still not only not fixed, but getting the company to show up and do it has become a nightmare for my wife, who is running point at home.

It’s enraging. We’re now weeks into this situation without a resolution, and my patience has officially run out.

Instead of spending some blue-collar money one last time at the tables, I’m now dealing with this issue and then I run into a major computer problem.

What seemed like a successful trip is unraveling into a nightmare as I sit on the one-yard line waiting to punch the ball in.

You remember the start about a fight for your soul? I successfully avoided detection in Las Vegas (major win), clawed back some losses to an acceptable point (huge win) and was ready to roll one last time.

One final engagement at the tables.

Instead I’m in a hotel room dealing with infuriating nonsense.

It’s not the bright moments when you have to remember to save your soul. It’s the dark ones, and that’s what I’m left doing as the clock ticks down.

I eventually get enough of it smoothed out, but now I have to race to catch my plane. With a Burger King burger and some fries in my stomach, it’s time to go home.

I spent five days dancing with the demons, battling the highest stakes I’ve ever gambled and made it out alive.

Little did I know the biggest fight yet was only hours away.

In the final stretch of my plane ride home I start to notice something that I don’t think many other people are:

The plane is flying in a holding pattern.

We’re not getting any closer to our final destination. We’re holding.

A brief holding pattern is one thing. A holding pattern that carries on for an extended period of time is rarely a good thing.

Then the pilot comes over the PA system and gives us all the devastating news. The plane is being diverted to a completely different airport due to the final destination having a ground closure.

You have to be kidding me, right? I just made it out of Las Vegas alive and am supposed to be landing back home in minutes.

Instead, we’re bound for an airport much further away from my home, and while that’s bad enough, what’s looming is an experience so hellish that I can only pray I never have to repeat it again.

Once the plane lands, we’re just stuck on a runway for hours. It feels like Lord of the Flies. Discontent is growing. Now, I will say none of this is the fault of the crew. I’m not blaming them. I’m blaming the universe.
